issues.detail: The Greek 'εκβαλω' (ekballō) means 'cast out' or 'throw out,' but the Vietnamese translation uses 'lấy ... ra' (take ... out), which is a milder action. More importantly, the Greek 'δοκος' (dokos) refers to a 'beam' or 'timber' (a large piece of wood), whereas the Vietnamese 'cây đà' usually refers to a 'crossbar' or 'support beam,' which may slightly narrow the scope of the original object.
